segments.text: Hello, and welcome all of you to the library tour.
It's so lovely to see you first years here at UE.
I hope you'll have a once-in-a-lifetime experience studying at our university.
Now, before we start our tour, I'd like to give you some ideas about what we have here at French Library.
The library has four levels, each of which has their own functions.
Level one is the help zone.
You can find help from our staff at the help desk, as well as borrow and return items using the self-service machines.
There used to be vending machines here selling coffee and snacks for those in need during exam time,
but they were moved to the corridor just outside the turnstiles.
What if you're thirsty but don't wish to go out?
There are drinking fountains by the stairs at every level.
You might want to bring your own water bottle if you don't want to move back
and forth though. If you need printing, scanning, or photocopying materials, there
are two print hubs at level 1 and 3. Level 2 is the quiet zone, but our
students often refer to it as the tech zone because you can borrow laptops, book
an assistive technology room, or take advantage of two-screen computers to
help you study, especially for design and programming students. If you wish to
study alone, head straight to level four, the silent zone. We have multiple study
pods with individual desk lamps for you there. The law library and research zone
are also located there for law and postgraduate students. If you have to do
a team presentation and need to work together, level 3 is for you. There are bookable rooms
with built-in projectors so your team can practice your presentation and see how the
project progresses. Articles from academic journals and magazines can also be found here.
